head: d601fdd34
scope: Code-static audit of validation, persistence, pricing, rendering paths for 8 extreme order shapes never previously tested.
discipline: Code-static + sample API POST acceptable. No DB pollution (no 999-qty/30-item orders ringed up).

scenarios.name: Very long order (30 items)
scenarios.evidence: ValidJsonOrder rule (app/Rules/ValidJsonOrder.php) only validates each entry has item_id>0 + quantity>0 + instruction<=500 chars. NO max items[] cap. PosOrderRequest.rules() line 115 only validates items as JSON string, no array sizing rule. PricingService::calculateOrder iterates requestItems with no upper bound, builds composition_snapshot per line. order_items table accepts 30 rows trivially (no constraint). composition_snapshot is per-row json column (MySQL ~4GB max). PHP memory_limit=128M, post_max_size=8M — a 30-item payload with full composer snapshots (~30 x ~50KB worst case = 1.5MB) fits comfortably.

rendering_paths.receipt: posReceiptBuilder.js iterates item_variations/item_extras/item_addons line-by-line — no truncation, ESC/POS will simply print multi-page ticket.
rendering_paths.kds_card: KdsOrderCard.vue body has overflow-y: auto + scrollbar-thin (line 574-585), so 30 items scroll inside the card. Wave U 2026-05-21 explicitly added darker scrollbar hint for long-item orders.
rendering_paths.kds_line: KdsOrderLine.vue clamps each item name to 2 lines (-webkit-line-clamp: 2), supplement to 2 lines.

scenarios.performance_concern: No N+1 in PricingService — DB queries are batched (whereIn for variations/extras/addons), so 30 items = same query count as 3 items. Composition_snapshot json_encode per line is O(n). Acceptable.
scenarios.concern: No items[] count cap → DoS surface (a typo/bad client could POST 10k items). At ~50KB per snapshot the 8MB post_max_size hard-stops at ~160 items, but Laravel would return 413 silently. Suggest a soft cap (e.g. items.* max:80) for defense-in-depth.

scenarios.name: Item with 50 ingredients (variations+extras+addons)
scenarios.evidence: CompositionSnapshotBuilder::build (app/Services/Pricing/CompositionSnapshotBuilder.php:29-175) iterates item_variations / item_extras / item_addons unbounded; each becomes a structured array entry (~200B). 50 ingredients = ~10KB snapshot, well below MySQL JSON ~4GB. PricingService::assertVariationConstraints respects per-attribute min_select / max_select but no global ingredient ceiling.

rendering_paths.receipt: normalizeReceiptVariations / Extras / Addons (posReceiptBuilder.js:157-249) all return flat arrays. ESC/POS print spool unaffected.
rendering_paths.kds_line: Each variation rendered as separate line inside KdsOrderLine (-webkit-line-clamp:2). 50 lines = card scrolls. UX trade-off but no break.

scenarios.performance_concern: Item attribute / extra / addon queries are still batched via whereIn — 50 ingredients on ONE item = 3 SELECT queries total. Negligible.

scenarios.name: Very long item name (200 chars)
scenarios.evidence: ItemRequest.rules() (app/Http/Requests/ItemRequest.php:42-46) enforces 'name' max:190 via Laravel validation. Admin UI cannot post 200 chars. HOWEVER: items.name DB column is varchar(255) — a name seeded directly via tinker/import/migration could exceed 190. The 200-char value would survive in DB and propagate to receipt + KDS + tracker without explicit length-guard.

rendering_paths.kds_line: KdsOrderLine.vue line 163-166: -webkit-line-clamp:2 + overflow:hidden — 200-char name truncates visually to 2 lines (~120 chars at clamp(22px)). NO ellipsis explicitly set but webkit adds one.
rendering_paths.receipt: ReceiptComponent.vue / posReceiptBuilder.js use {{ item.item_name }} verbatim. 58mm thermal = ~32 chars/line, 80mm = ~48. A 200-char name will wrap to 4-7 lines on the printed ticket. Ugly but not broken.
rendering_paths.cart: PosComponent.vue cart-item uses default flex layout; 200-char name will wrap unless container has explicit truncate class.

scenarios.concern: Idempotency-key generation does NOT include item.name — search OrderService::posOrderStore confirms name is read but not hashed into the X-Idempotency-Key path. So a long name does NOT change duplicate-detection behaviour. Safe.

scenarios.name: Quantity = 999
scenarios.evidence: ValidJsonOrder.php:60 only checks quantity > 0 (no upper bound). PosOrderRequest has no items.*.quantity rule. PricingService line 232: $verifiedQuantity = max(1, (int) ($item->quantity ?? 1)) — accepts 999. DB column order_items.quantity is signed INT (max 2,147,483,647). decimal(19,6) total_price holds up to 9.99 trillion. Cart UI PosComponent.vue:3441-3448 accepts any integer >0. Receipt prints '999 x ...'. NF525 sequence allocated regardless.

rendering_paths.receipt: qty printed as integer — '999×' fits the 7-char wide column (ReceiptComponent.vue:295 'w-7').
rendering_paths.kds: KdsOrderLine renders quantity badge; 3-digit fits common 56px qty bubble.

scenarios.stock_concern: No stock_levels decrement overflow check observed. If branch stock < 999 the AvailabilityService::assertItemsOrderableForBranch should throw 422 (preview path uses non-locking read). For items not stock-tracked, no guard.
scenarios.concern: No per-line quantity cap → a typo could ring up a 99999€ order, NF525-sealed (cannot be deleted). Suggest hard cap items.*.quantity max:99 (UX) or max:999 (insurance) in PosOrderRequest + ValidJsonOrder.

scenarios.name: Discount = 100% (free order, total=0€)
scenarios.evidence: PricingService line 355: $finalTotal = $req->roundFinalOrderTotal ? round(max(0.0, $rawTotal), 2) : max(0.0, $rawTotal); — explicitly clamps total to >=0. OrderService::posOrderStore line 963/965 also wraps in max(0, ...). composition_snapshot per-line still records original unit_price / line_total (CompositionSnapshotBuilder lines 76-78, 99-101, 159-160) — NF525 immutable trace preserved. PosOrderRequest line 103 already permits total min:0 with explicit AUDIT-P50-BUG4 comment ('server allows total=0 for 100% loyalty redemption'). PaymentTerminal CARD breakdown.*.amount has min:0.01 — but CASH/CASH-only path with total=0 has no min check.
scenarios.fiscal_path: FiscalSequenceService::next(branchId) (app/Services/Fiscal/FiscalSequenceService.php:57) is unconditional — branchId>0 allocates next sequence regardless of total amount. Free order IS a fiscal event. Verified PASS.
scenarios.audit_path: AuditLogService::signEvent computes HMAC over payload, no amount-based skip. Order with total=0 still produces an audit_logs row.

scenarios.name: Cart total > 1000€ (e.g. 1234.56€)
scenarios.evidence: Frontend: helpers/formatPrice.js uses Intl.NumberFormat('fr-FR', {style:'currency', currency:'EUR'}). fr-FR locale natively produces '1 234,56 €' with NBSP (\u202F narrow no-break space) thousands separator. Backend: AppLibrary::currencyAmountFormat (app/Libraries/AppLibrary.php:271-304) uses NumberFormatter::CURRENCY with fr_FR locale (G2-HEAL-02 fix 2026-05-23) — same FR-canonical output. Receipt + emails + reports converge bit-for-bit.
scenarios.tpe_simulation: POS_SIMULATION_HARDWARE bypass returns success without amount check (NF525 production boot guard at AppServiceProvider.php:78-145 forbids simulation in production). Simulation accepts any amount. Real TPE would have its own per-merchant cap (typically 1500-5000€ contactless, unlimited contact+PIN) — out of code scope.

rendering_paths.receipt: ESC/POS thermal line is 32-48 chars wide; '1 234,56 €' = 11 chars — fits trivially.
rendering_paths.kds: Total not shown on KDS card (kitchen-facing); irrelevant.

scenarios.name: Cart total = 0.01€
scenarios.evidence: PricingService and PosOrderRequest enforce min:0 NOT min:0.01 — so 0.01€ orders are accepted. payment_breakdown.*.amount has min:0.01 (PosOrderRequest:142) which is the lowest tranche allowed. Fiscal sequence allocated normally. audit_logs row written.
scenarios.tpe_concern: Real TPE hardware often rejects below 0.50€ (merchant config). Code does not pre-check this — a 0.01€ CARD order would fail at TPE physical level with no client-side guard. Acceptable for V1 LOCAL (cash) but flag for V2.
scenarios.concern: decimal(19,6) precision means 0.01€ stores as 0.010000 — round-trip safe. NumberFormat displays '0,01 €' correctly. No float precision issue at this magnitude.

scenarios.name: Loyalty redeem covers full order (50€ redeem on 50€ subtotal)
scenarios.evidence: PosRedemptionService::applyToOrder (app/Services/Loyalty/PosRedemptionService.php:131) guards: if ($discountEur > $subtotal) throw — STRICT >, so discount EQUAL to subtotal passes. Line 192-193: $newDiscount = round($currentDiscount + $discountEur, 2); $newTotal = round($subtotal - $newDiscount + $currentTax + $currentDelivery, 2).
scenarios.tax_inclusive_interaction: CRITICAL: config('pricing.tax_inclusive_prices')=true by DEFAULT (config/pricing.php:31, env PRICING_TAX_INCLUSIVE=true). When TTC mode: order.total = sum(TTC lines) + delivery - discount (NO tax added separately). PosRedemptionService line 193 adds $currentTax back in — but in TTC mode order.total_tax is the EXTRACTED tax (already inside subtotal). This would DOUBLE-COUNT tax in the recomputation: total = subtotal[TTC] - discount + tax[already in TTC] + delivery. RESULT: free order (50€ subtotal, 50€ redeem) would land at total = 50 - 50 + 5 + 0 = 5€ instead of 0€. INVESTIGATE.
scenarios.composition_snapshot: PASS — composition_snapshot is built at order CREATION (PricingService L266-291), BEFORE PosRedemptionService runs on existing order. Original unit_price / line_total per ingredient is sealed. Redemption only mutates order.discount + order.total. NF525 trace preserved.
scenarios.receipt: OrderDetailsResource exposes order.discount + order.loyalty_customer_code; ReceiptComponent.vue renders discount line. PASS.
scenarios.fiscal_sequence: Already allocated at order creation. Redemption mutates discount/total post-allocation — sequence_no untouched. PASS.

edge_failures.scenario: H5.4 quantity=999 with no business cap
edge_failures.impact: Cashier typo could ring up 99999€ order, fiscal-sealed, irreversible (only refund/avoir possible). Frozen-zone item composition_snapshot also bloats line.
edge_failures.recommendation: Add 'items.*.quantity' => 'max:99' (or 999) in PosOrderRequest + extend ValidJsonOrder to enforce. UX: warn at qty>20.

edge_failures.impact: Malicious/buggy client could POST 1000-item payload, exhaust 8MB post_max_size (silent 413), or worse — if PHP limits raised, allocate >128M memory on snapshot build, triggering OOM.
edge_failures.recommendation: Extend ValidJsonOrder to enforce count(decoded) <= 80 (or config('orders.max_items_per_order')). Reject early with explicit message.

edge_failures.scenario: H5.8 PosRedemptionService::applyToOrder potentially double-counts tax in TTC mode
edge_failures.impact: Free-order redemption (50€ subtotal, 50€ redeem) might recompute total=5€ instead of 0€ when tax_inclusive_prices=true (V1 default). Would mean: customer charged 5€ on a 100%-loyalty-paid order, NF525-sealed. Requires runtime verification with a real subtotal/total_tax pair.
edge_failures.recommendation: Mirror PricingService L350-354 TTC branch inside PosRedemptionService::applyToOrder L193: if config('pricing.tax_inclusive_prices') then total = subtotal - newDiscount + delivery (NO tax). Add regression test PosRedemption_FreeOrder_TaxInclusive_Test.

edge_failures.scenario: H5.7 0.01€ orders accepted but real TPE may reject
edge_failures.impact: 0.01€ CARD order fails at TPE hardware with no friendly client guard.
edge_failures.recommendation: Optional V2: add config('payments.min_card_amount', 0.50) gate in PosOrderRequest withValidator.

edge_failures.scenario: H5.3 item name 200 chars surviving via direct DB seed/import
edge_failures.impact: Visual layout pressure on receipt (4-7 wrap lines). KDS clamps to 2 lines without explicit ellipsis fallback (relies on webkit). Cart could overflow.
edge_failures.recommendation: Add DB-level constraint or model boot() validator to clamp to 190 chars on save. Add explicit text-overflow: ellipsis to KDS line as defense-in-depth.

performance_impact: H.5.1 30 items: 1 batched query each for items+variations+extras+addons+attributes (5 SELECT total via whereIn). composition_snapshot built in PHP loop — O(n). Acceptable on Le Cayenne single-branch.
H.5.2 50 ingredients on 1 item: 0 additional DB queries (loaded inside the parent batched query). PASS.
H.5.4 qty=999: zero performance impact (single arithmetic mul).
H.5.6 >1000€: zero performance impact (decimal(19,6) precision native).
non_blocking_observations: PHP defaults observed locally: max_input_vars=1000 (irrelevant — items is JSON string), memory_limit=128M, post_max_size=8M. Le Cayenne LOCAL ship-ready unless 80+ extreme-composer items in a single order is a realistic flow (it isn't).
NumberFormatter (PHP ext-intl) is REQUIRED for canonical 1234.56€ -> '1 234,56 €' rendering on PHP side. AppLibrary line 291 has manual fallback. Verify ext-intl present in Le Cayenne prod box.
Loyalty redeem PosRedemptionService.php:131 strict > check is INCLUSIVE of equality — subtotal=50, discount=50 PASSES (the >= boundary case is safe).
top_3_concerns_summary: EDGE-3 P1-INVESTIGATE: PosRedemptionService may double-count tax in TTC mode when recomputing total after redemption — verify against a real {subtotal, total_tax} pair. If confirmed, a free-order redemption charges the customer the tax slice instead of 0€.
EDGE-1 P2: No quantity cap anywhere — items.*.quantity > 99 fiscal-sealed without prompt. Cashier-typo NF525-blast surface.
EDGE-2 P2: No items[] count cap — silent post_max_size 413 truncation, possible OOM if PHP limits raised. Suggest config-driven max:80.
verdict_rationale: All 8 scenarios technically functional under V1 LOCAL Le Cayenne single-branch use. PASS: H5.2, H5.5, H5.6. PASS-WITH-CONCERN: H5.1, H5.4, H5.7. AMBER: H5.3 (admin-form blocks at 190 but DB-direct seeds survive). PASS-with-LATENT-BUG: H5.8 (tax-inclusive recompute path needs runtime verification to confirm/deny the double-count). NF525 fiscal invariants survive every scenario (composition_snapshot sealed at creation, fiscal_sequence_no allocated unconditionally, audit_logs chain intact). Frontend rendering (KDS scroll, receipt iteration, currency format) all degrade gracefully. Three V1.0.2 backlog candidates surfaced: explicit items/quantity caps + PosRedemptionService TTC-aware total recompute.
